compliance.intro: The matrix is derived from the model: properties, the mitigations of the risk treatment, supporting measures outside the component, your statements and claims. Unset properties count as unknown — never as not applicable.
compliance.deviceProposal: Proposal from the model: {{categories}} — confirm before the device rows count.
compliance.deviceAsk: Choose the device category of the component — workstation or mobile device: HDR if the device is delivered, SAR for an app or tool only.
compliance.modelUnknown: model still open — information missing on {{elements}}
compliance.metModelOpen: Met by the {{source}}. The model alone does not show it yet — see the elements below; once their properties meet the requirement, the model does too.
compliance.contradiction: Mitigation marked done, but the model shows the requirement not met.
compliance.modelChanged: The model changed since the statement — review it.
compliance.statementModel: Model result now: {{status}}. It is stored with the statement, so a later change of the model is shown.
compliance.supportingMeasureHelp: Name it when the system around the component meets the requirement (CCSC 2).
compliance.noClaim: No claim — when the system around the component provides the requirement, claim it here.
compliance.unlinkClaim: Remove the claim from this requirement
compliance.claimTitle: Claim: the system provides the requirement
compliance.claimHelp: Name the measure of the system around the component (CCSC 2, supporting measure) and who provides it — the operator, the integrator or another component. A claimed requirement counts for the value with measures of the system, not for SL-C of the product.
compliance.noModel: The requirement matrix needs a data flow diagram — model the system in the DFD tab first.
compliance.vectorText: SL-T: what the operator or the zone requires. SL-C (product): what the product provides according to the model; planned: after the chosen open mitigations. With measures of the system: what the plant can reach if it provides the listed supporting measures and claims — the basis for the SL-A, which only arises in the operated plant.
compliance.summaryDisclaimer: Summary in our own words — the standard is authoritative.
compliance.guideTitle: How to work with this tab
compliance.guide1: Choose the component under evaluation — or keep the whole model.
compliance.guide2: Set the SL-T per foundational requirement: what the operator, the zone or your customer requires.
compliance.guide3: Work through the to-do list: set the missing properties in the DFD, and choose mitigations in the risk treatment where the model shows a requirement not met.
compliance.guide4: Rows the model cannot show need a statement: reasoning and where the evidence is (manual, test report). Click a requirement number for everything about it.
compliance.guide5: Compare SL-C (product) with the SL-T: planned shows the value once the chosen mitigations are done; a gap that remains needs a change of the product or a measure of the system around it.
compliance.guideSrsl: There is no target to set: the SRSL comes from the rated risks in the risk tab, and the requirements apply to the whole machine.
compliance.srslTitle: SRSL per safety function and requirements per status
compliance.noSafetyFunctions: No safety function yet — mark the safety functions as assets with a physical impact.
compliance.todoTitle: To do up to the SL-T
compliance.todoNoTarget: Set the SL-T above — the to-do list shows what is open up to it.
compliance.todoNothing: Nothing open up to the SL-T.
compliance.todoRisks: In the risk tab — rate the risk or choose the mandated control
compliance.todoProject: In the project data — hazards, overview, item definition
compliance.todoComponent: For the component — one element suffices
compliance.todoInside: set its inside fields (black box), model its processes and stores on a child page, or make a statement

voidReason.voidInPraa: The CRA edition (EN IEC 62443-4-2/prAA) declares this requirement void — it does not apply to the component.
voidReason.noComponentRequirement: The standard sets no component requirement under this number — the topic is left to the system (IEC 62443-3-3).
voidReason.noComponentRequirementSr23: The standard sets no component requirement under this number — SR 2.3 is a system requirement (IEC 62443-3-3).
voidReason.noComponentRequirementPower: The standard sets no component requirement under this number — emergency power is a matter of the system (IEC 62443-3-3).

compliance.deleteClaim: Delete this unused claim for good
